title: Raw identity and composition coherence of objectwise fibre pullback
statement: Let k,l,R be as in [lem-per-normalized-pullback-objects]. Fix normalized fibres ω and an objectwise package p satisfying that node’s unit and integral local normalization. The raw identity R.identity.raw and raw composition R.composition.raw restrict to standard-heart isomorphisms e. Under those exact isomorphisms, p at the identity is ω(e), and p at h≫g is ω(e) followed by p_h and p_g. All equations are the HEq equations in the Lean attachment, retaining the actual raw comparison components. This concerns the coherence of an already given objectwise family and asserts no such family exists.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6); Remark 6.8.15; finite pullback stalk normalization, Stacks Tag 03Q1, etale-cohomology.tex lemma-stalk-pullback(3)

proof.text: Restrict the actual raw identity and composition isomorphisms of R to the full standard hearts, which are preserved by pullback. Fullness retains exactly their underlying raw components. Under J, compatibility with the normalized derived counits identifies these with the ordinary module inverse-image unit and compositor.

At each positive reduction level, identity sends the germ of a pulled section to itself. For h then g the twice-pulled germ is sent by both candidate comparisons to the original germ. The colimit description of finite etale stalks says these germs generate, so the maps agree under the ordinary inverse-image compositor. The completed-system comparisons retain their prescribed finite unit and composition equations.

Take inverse limits: equality follows under every limit projection. Rationalize the equality and use the local-normalization clauses of p, then cancel the common intrinsic fibre identifications. The J compatibility in the first step makes the resulting comparisons exactly the specified raw ones, proving both equations. Empty strata and rank zero obey the same statements.

lean.statement:
theorem objectwise_normalized_pullback_coherence
    (ω : Fibres (k := k) l R) (p : ObjectwiseNormalizedPullback l R ω) :
    (∀ (A : Type u) [Field A] [Algebra ℚ_[l] A]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] A] (X : FiniteTypeBase k),
    ∃ e : heartPull l A R (𝟙 X.scheme) ≅ 𝟭 _,
      (∀ F, HEq (e.hom.app F).hom ((R.identity A (base l X)).raw.hom.app F.obj)) ∧
      ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [IsAlgClosed κ] (x : Spec (.of κ) ⟶ X.scheme)
        (F : NormalizedFibre.Heart l A (base l X)),
        HEq ((p.component A (𝟙 X.scheme) κ x F).hom)
          (((ω A X).point κ x).functor.map (e.hom.app F))) ∧
    (∀ (A : Type u) [Field A] [Algebra ℚ_[l] A]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] A] (X Y Z : FiniteTypeBase k)
    (g : Y.scheme ⟶ X.scheme) (h : Z.scheme ⟶ Y.scheme),
    ∃ e : heartPull l A R (h ≫ g) ≅ heartPull l A R g ⋙ heartPull l A R h,
      (∀ F, HEq (e.hom.app F).hom
        ((R.composition A (X := base l Y) (Y := base l X) (Z := base l Z) g h).raw.hom.app
          F.obj)) ∧
      ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [IsAlgClosed κ] (z : Spec (.of κ) ⟶ Z.scheme)
        (F : NormalizedFibre.Heart l A (base l X)),
        HEq ((p.component A (h ≫ g) κ z F).hom)
          (((ω A Z).point κ z).functor.map (e.hom.app F) ≫
            (p.component A h κ z ((heartPull l A R g).obj F)).hom ≫
              (p.component A g κ (z ≫ h) F).hom))
